title: Delete the low-depth null-move verification re-search; add SEE and delta pruning to quiescence
hypothesis: The engine's measured effective branching factor is 4.22 against 1.6-2.0 for a well-tuned engine. Two structural causes, both in code that fires constantly at the depths a 150 ms search actually reaches: (1) a null-move fail-high at depth <= 12 was re-verified at FULL depth d-1, i.e. R=0, so a successful null prune cost a near-full-width subtree -- most of what null-move pruning exists to save; (2) quiescence, which is 92.7% of all nodes, expanded every capture with no SEE filter and no delta margin, and roughly a third of those captures are provably losing exchanges.
changes: PieBot/src/search/alphabeta_temp.rs null_move_probe: on a fail-high with depth <= 12, return the reduced score directly instead of re-searching at full depth d-1. The high-depth (> 12) reduced verification is unchanged. Zugzwang cover is already provided, and more directly, by should_try_null_move's pieces-only material floor, occupancy floor and is_zugzwang_prone check.

PieBot/src/search/alphabeta_temp.rs qsearch: skip captures with see_gain_cp < 0, and delta-prune non-promotions whose stand-pat plus the victim's value plus a 200 cp margin still fails to reach alpha. Both filters are disabled while in check, where the move list is evasions and every one must be searched.

PREREQUISITE, landed separately as commit e082812: see_gain_cp mis-valued en passant by a pawn (victim read off the empty destination square) and valued a promotion's post-move occupant as a pawn. Without that fix the SEE filter would silently discard every defended en-passant capture.

baseline_accept.note: was 20110404 before the SEE fix; the SEE fix is shared by both arms and slightly improves ordering

acceptance.note: accept and accept_temp use different option sets, so each is compared against its own history, per CLAUDE.md.

screen_400_games.hardware: Apple M-series, release build, 12 cores, 10 parallel opening-pair workers
screen_400_games.interpretation: NPS falls 17.7% because qsearch now runs a SEE per capture, and depth still rises 0.81 ply at equal time -- the node-count reduction more than pays for the filter. For scale, the previously banked arms had mean pair deltas of +0.206 (S1), +0.12 (S2) and +0.058 (S3).

promotion.criterion: CLAUDE.md: paired-bootstrap 95% LCB > 0 over 1000 games after a 400-game screen. LCB = +0.252.
promotion.comparison_to_banked_arms: Mean pair delta +0.32 against S1 +0.206, S2 +0.12, S3 +0.058 -- larger than all three combined.

accept_temp.note: equals the experimental arm's signature, confirming the promotion copied faithfully; alphabeta_temp.rs is back to the re-export stub

promotion.full_battery: cargo test --locked --all-targets green; python unittest discover over training/nnue/tests (248) and scripts/tests (92) green.

attribution_caveat: This arm bundles two independent changes, so the split between them is NOT measured. They were bundled because both were independently measured as large node-count reductions in an isolated worktree (null-verify deletion 2.43x, qsearch SEE+delta 3.74x at fixed depth 8) and the campaign has limited box time. If a per-change number is ever needed, run each separately against the same baseline.
provenance: Found by a multi-agent audit of the search on 2026-08-11 that measured EBF directly (4.22 over depths 6-11) rather than inferring it, then built an isolated git worktree to measure each candidate change's node-count effect before any was proposed.
